title: DEVOPS↔BIZ-001: Infrastructure Cost vs Business Budget + Reliability/SLA Metrics
description: The DevOps/Platform Engineer provides platform-infrastructure operational-cost estimates and reliability/uptime metrics that affect customer SLA (Service-Level Agreement) commitments and contract terms; the Business Consultant provides the business SLA requirements that drive infrastructure-reliability investment and the cost-budget constraints for CI/CD (Continuous Integration / Continuous Delivery) and platform tooling. Grounded in DEVOPS_PLATFORM_ENGINEER_SKILL §6.10. ASYMMETRY: BUSINESS_CONSULTANT_SKILL §6 has no DevOps subsection, so this contract is documented one-sided from the DevOps card; the §6.10 Provides/Requires pair documents both directions (DevOps Provides = what BIZ requires; DevOps Requires = what BIZ provides), so reciprocity is reconstructed from the single grounded side — this is grounded, NOT a DERIVED/invented contract.

infra_cost_reliability_package.description: DEVOPS→BIZ: infrastructure OpEx estimate, reliability/uptime metrics affecting customer SLA.

affects_customer_sla.description: True when the metric bears on a customer SLA commitment or contract term.

business_infra_inputs.description: BIZ→DEVOPS: business SLA requirements driving reliability investment, cost-budget constraints for CI/CD and platform tooling.

x-macp.tier_rationale: Routine infrastructure-cost and reliability reporting against business SLA targets is agent-autonomous (GTM planning; quarterly operational review). A reliability metric below a committed customer SLA, or an OpEx projection over the business budget, is surfaced as a trade — not silently absorbed.
x-macp.source_status: ASYMMETRIC — grounded one-sided from DEVOPS §6.10 (no BIZ §6 DevOps subsection); reciprocity reconstructed from the single documented side, not invented.
x-macp.cadence: TRIGGER + CALENDAR (at GTM planning; quarterly operational review)
confirm_conditions: infrastructure OpEx and CI/CD tooling costs carry value, currency, and unit
reliability uptime carries its % unit; business SLA targets carry explicit units
metrics bearing on a customer SLA commitment are flagged (affects_customer_sla)
OpEx is reported against the business cost-budget constraint for comparison
reject_conditions: a cost, uptime, or SLA quantity emitted without a unit (units rule §3.10)
a reliability metric below a committed business SLA presented as meeting SLA (Honesty Over Polish §10.3)
infrastructure OpEx over the business budget presented as within budget without flagging the trade (Never-Silently-Deviate)
counter_conditions: a business SLA target requires reliability investment beyond the stated budget — request a budget or SLA-scope decision
an SLA metric is specified without a measurable target — request a quantified target before the reliability-investment assessment
